question_type: 3-year centered moving average of a derived ratio (customs duties / value of dutiable imports) across fiscal years, with a qualifier ('goods subject to duty') narrower than the table's printed totals

opus_path.decision: Rate = duties collected on dutiable goods / value of dutiable goods, per fiscal year; a 3-term centered moving average over FY1939-41 is one value centered on FY1940 = simple mean of the three annual rates; report as a decimal fraction to 3 places.

Searched for a published duty-rate / ratio column (none exists anywhere) and for a duties-only table (the Revenue-Act tax table stops before FY1941), so the rate must be computed from 'Customs Duties and Taxes Collected, and Values of Dutiable and Taxable Imports, Estimated by Tariff Schedules'.

Read the table structure and footnote 3/: the 'Free list' block is duty-free commodities that only pay Revenue-Act taxes, so it is NOT 'subject to duty'. Formula = (Total duties and taxes - Total free list) / (Total value - Free-list value).

No issue prints all three fiscal years; 1941_02-1941_08 issues print calendar years (avoid). FY1939 from the latest revision (1941_01; the 1939_09 preliminary print is superseded), FY1940/FY1941 from 1941_11 (clean OCR). OCR glitches in 1941_09/1941_12/1940_10/1940_11 resolved by cross-issue agreement.
For each FY, summed the 16 dutiable tariff-schedule rows and checked they equal total-minus-free-list (fixing two OCR digit slips against other issues).
Computed the three rates and their mean in calc.py; sensitivity: the preliminary FY1939 print gives the same rounded result; including the free list gives a different value, explicitly rejected.
Decimal fraction rounded to thousandths (question has no percent sign).
Reviewer re-opened source lines, re-checked the free-list footnote reading and recomputed (both mean-of-ratios and pooled ratio round the same).

opus_key_moves: Mapped the qualifier 'goods subject to duty' onto the table via footnote 3/ and subtracted the duty-free 'Free list' rows from BOTH numerator and denominator instead of using the printed grand totals
Validated the derived dutiable totals by summing the 16 tariff-schedule rows for every fiscal year
Assembled the three fiscal years from the right issues (latest revision for FY1939; avoided the calendar-year printings)

first_divergence.what_glm_did: Used 'Total duties and taxes' / 'Total value of dutiable and taxable imports' (grand totals, which include the duty-free Free list) for each FY, then averaged the three rates.
first_divergence.what_opus_did: Subtracted the Free list (duty-free goods taxed under the Revenue Act, footnote 3/) from both numerator and denominator, because such goods are not 'subject to duty'.
first_divergence.why_glm_went_that_way: It saw the issue at [22] ('"goods subject to duty" maybe ... excludes taxable free list?'), computed the correct exclusion variant at [55], and at [56] even stated the free list is 'duty-free commodities taxed under Revenue Act. So yes.' It then talked itself back: the phrase is 'generated by question writer, not source. They likely don't expect adjusting free list' and at [73] concluded 'goods subject to duty includes taxable free list'. The choice defaulted to the printed total row.
first_divergence.consequence: All three annual rates are computed on the wrong base; the mean lands on the rejected alternative Opus recorded (a few percent below the reference).

right_arms_note: No arm was right. All three reached the same table and the same (correct) FY vintages; all three failed at the same interpretation fork (printed totals vs excluding the duty-free Free list), and two also 'verified' with a check (mean-of-ratios vs pooled ratio) that is blind to that fork.
text_vs_mechanism: Probably needs a mechanism: every arm had the footnote on screen and the none arm even computed the right variant, then rationalized the printed total; the prompt arm had generic 'write the convention' text and still failed. A forced candidate-comparison/qualifier-coverage step (CONTROL) or a label-vs-qualifier reviewer (CHECK) targets the actual failure; a dedicated text lesson might help but is untested.
notes: Recurring pattern: the actor treats question wording as a loose paraphrase of table labels ('generated by question writer') and defaults to the grand total, even when a footnote shows a component is excluded by the qualifier. Also: the verification the arms did perform (two averaging methods agree) is orthogonal to the error. index.json marks the reference's structured answer (which carried a decimal plus a percent in parentheses) as 0 while the bare final is 1, consistent with the none arm's count_mismatch: single-number format enforcement matters for this grader. Large share of every run was spent grepping for a verbatim question phrase that does not exist in the corpus.
